patch.objective: Explain confidentiality and privileged communication, their limits, and how HIPAA protects health information
secondaryObjectives: Keep accurate, relevant records and bill only for services provided, by the person who provided them

sources.cite: RCW 70.02.060 (1991 c 335 s 205): before serving a discovery request or compulsory process for health care information, the requester gives the provider and the patient advance notice with a date to seek a protective order, 'in no event' less than fourteen days; without that notice, 'Without the written consent of the patient, the health care provider may not disclose'; complying does not waive any privilege
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the Legislature's PDF of the section (summarizing fetch with the short quotes given).

sources.cite: HHS, HIPAA FAQ 706, What satisfactory assurances must a covered entity receive before it responds to a subpoena? A subpoena not accompanied by a court order allows disclosure only with written satisfactory assurances that the individual was given notice and the time to object passed, or that a qualified protective order was sought (45 CFR 164.512(e))
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on hhs.gov (summarizing fetch with short quotes).

sources.cite: NASW Code of Ethics (2021 revision): 1.02 self-determination, limited when clients' actions 'pose a serious, foreseeable, and imminent risk to themselves or others'; 1.03(c)-(d); 1.07(c) minimum necessary; 1.07(d) notice before disclosure; 1.07(j) court orders: ask the court to withdraw or limit the order or keep records under seal; 1.14; 1.17(a)-(b)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on socialworkers.org (summarizing fetch with short quotes; the page shows the 2021 code). Amendments were to be voted 2026-11-18; recheck by 2026-12-15.

sources.cite: Chapter 70.02 RCW as the Washington jurisprudence course records it: 70.02.030 (a valid authorization is in writing, dated and signed, names the information, the recipient and the patient, and has an expiration date or event); 70.02.230 (mental health records stay confidential except as the chapter allows)

brief.situation: You are a licensed social worker at a Washington family counseling agency. Karen Liu, 36 (a fictional client), has seen you for six months for depression after her divorce. This morning a subpoena arrived from her ex-husband's attorney for 'any and all records' of her services, for a custody modification hearing, to be produced in ten days. It is a subpoena signed by the attorney, not an order signed by a judge, and nothing with it shows that Karen was given notice. Karen's session is now. You have 50 minutes.
